messages.content: Write the opening pitch section of a README for a new open source charting library. Around 200 words.

Passes the repo's own `slopwatch` gate. ~200 words:

---

# Plotwright

Most charting libraries make the easy chart easy and the real one impossible. You get a bar chart in four lines, then lose two days when the y-axis needs a second scale and the tooltip needs a value the chart was never handed.

Plotwright turns that around. The bottom layer is a scale and layout engine — 11 kB gzipped, zero dependencies, no framework attached. Everything above it is optional: shorthand for the charts you draw every week, an SVG renderer, a Canvas renderer for the days you have 200,000 points and a scroll event. When the shorthand stops fitting, drop a layer. Nothing is private, and the layer below is always a plain function you can call yourself.

A chart here is a data structure, not a black box. You can inspect it, diff it, snapshot-test it in a Node process with no DOM. The chart type nobody has built yet is roughly forty lines against the same primitives the bundled ones use.

Written for people who ship charts that someone actually reads the numbers off.

---
